levels.label: א
levels.name: Alef
levels.guidance: Write for an end-of-Alef learner who can decode unpointed Hebrew. Keep the full developed story and aim for the unchanged target length using 4 short paragraphs and usually 12–18 short sentences. Prefer frequent concrete words, active clauses, simple verb forms, and one event or thought per sentence. Avoid passive or nominal phrasing, formal connectors, unnecessary foreign terms, dense construct chains, and nested clauses. Explain a necessary hard term immediately in simple words. Simplicity must come from wording and sentence shape, not from deleting events or making the version shorter. Keep the voice adult and natural.

levels.label: א+
levels.name: Alef Plus
levels.guidance: Write for advanced Alef in 4–5 paragraphs and normally 8–11 sentences. Use past tense, simple cause and effect, natural connectors, common fixed expressions, and limited subordinate clauses while keeping the story easy to follow.

levels.label: ב
levels.name: Bet
levels.guidance: Write 4–5 developed paragraphs of reasonably natural contemporary Hebrew, normally 9–12 sentences, with useful detail, causes, comparisons, reactions, and common colloquial constructions. Avoid dense journalistic syntax and specialist vocabulary.
